text:
alex: Heads up - saw a burst today where QPS for /generate jumped x6 for ~45s. HPA fired, pods scaled up, CA started new GPU nodes, then pods scaled down before nodes finished provisioning -> lots of preemptible churn and cost spike.
jamie: ugh. was that in us-west1?
alex: yes, us-west1-a. Mixed nodepool (on-demand + preemptible). CA logs show nodes created then marked NotReady for ~80s. pods got evicted once the preemptible provider reclaimed.
priya: do we still have VPA enabled on that deployment? VPA + HPA sometimes fights if VPA recommends resource increases.
alex: VPA is enabled but only in recommendation mode for that deployment. I checked — not the culprit. Main problem is metric staleness on custom QPS external metric and aggressive scaleDown/scaleUp settings.
sanjay: can you paste the HPA and external metrics config?
alex: sure: ```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: gen-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: generator
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 40
  metrics:
  - type: External
    external:
      metric:
        name: generator_qps
      target:
        type: AverageValue
        averageValue: 250
```
alex: Our external metrics adapter aggregates at 10s but the provider can flush in bursts. Means HPA sees a sharp spike then another drop.
jamie: so HPA spins up pods, CA starts nodes, but by the time nodes are Ready the HPA target may already be below threshold -> pods reschedule and nodes are underused.
priya: options: 1) increase HPA stabilization window and add scaleUp/down behavior; 2) buffer QPS with smoothing/rolling avg at adapter level; 3) ensure a warm pool of GPU nodes (min nodes in nodepool) or use burstable on-demand fallback.
sanjay: also look at CA config: increase `--scale-down-unneeded-time` and `--balance-similar-node-groups=false` maybe? and ensure `--node-group-auto-discovery` picks up reserved pools.
alex: proposal: moderate changes we can try quickly:
- make HPA use a 60s window avg (adapter side) and set `behavior` for stabilization.
- set nodepool min size to 2 GPUs for gen nodepool (warm pool) and mark those as on-demand (not preemptible).
- bump CA `--scale-down-unneeded-time` to 10m for that cluster to avoid premature scale down.
- add an admission webhook to prefer scheduling to on-demand nodes when QPS > 400 (nodeAffinity + taint toleration).
priya: sounds reasonable. Another lightweight change: have the metrics adapter emit a smoothed metric named `generator_qps_rolling` computed with e.g. 30s EWMA, keep `generator_qps` for alerting but HPA uses the smoothed one. That avoids messing with HPA internals.
jamie: good call. Cost tradeoff: warm on-demand nodes add baseline cost but reduce churn and egress from preemptible reclaim.
sanjay: also check pod disruption budgets and `maxUnavailable` for rollout - if we have PDB misconfigured, CA may evict too aggressively.
alex: I ran a dry run with HPA behavior set (scaleUp stabilization) and adapter smoothing and saw fewer node launches in staging. Will run a short canary in us-west1 next hour.
priya: can you open a small RFC with the exact CA flags + nodepool size change + adapter PR? i'll review.
alex: will do. action items: (1) alex -> PR for adapter smoothing + HPA to use `generator_qps_rolling`; (2) jamie -> create on-demand warm nodepool (min 2); (3) sanjay -> propose CA flag changes in RFC; (4) priya -> check PDBs and VPA modes. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-217333 - short QPS burst caused GPU node churn in us-west1. Link: https://incidents.internal/redwood/INC-2026-217333
jamie: adding one more ask - can we add a temporary cost alert to watch preemptible churn rate? I don't want another surprise bill.
alex: yep i'll add a billing alarm for >30% preemptible reprovisions/hour for that project.
priya: thanks all. keep updates in this thread. :white_check_mark:
